worship the Sun whose greatness is immeasurable,
dedicated to him, your intellects fixed on him, your actions given to him, having him as refuge,

1.61.s:
taddṛṣṭayastanmanasaḥ sarvasmintsa1 iti sthitāḥ .
samastānyatha karmāṇi tatra sarvātmanātmani . . 16
1.61.d:
तद्दृष्टयस्तन्मनसः सर्वस्मिन्त्स1 इति स्थिताः ।
समस्तान्यथ कर्माणि तत्र सर्वात्मनात्मनि ॥ 16
1.61.m:
your vision on him, your minds on him, standing with the conviction that he is in everything.
Then, with your whole self, surrender all actions

1.61.s:
saṃnyasadhvaṃ sa vaḥ karttā samastāvaraṇakṣayam .
etattadakṣaraṃ brahma pradhānapuruṣāvubhau . . 17
1.61.d:
संन्यसध्वं स वः कर्त्ता समस्तावरणक्षयम् ।
एतत्तदक्षरं ब्रह्म प्रधानपुरुषावुभौ ॥ 17
1.61.m:
unto the Self in him; he will bring about the destruction of all your coverings.
He is this imperishable brahman, and both nature [pradhāna] and the spirit [puruṣa];

1.61.s:
2yato yasminyathā cobhau sarvayyāpinyavasthitau .
paraḥ parāṇāṃ paramaḥ saikaḥ sumanasāṃ paraḥ . . 18
1.61.d:
2यतो यस्मिन्यथा चोभौ सर्वय्यापिन्यवस्थितौ ।
परः पराणां परमः सैकः सुमनसां परः ॥ 18
1.61.m:
from whom and in whom both abide, as he pervades all.
He is higher than the high, the supreme, the single highest [goal] of the pure-minded,

1.61.s:
yasmādbhinnamidaṃ sarvaṃ 3yaccedaṃ yacca neṅgati .
mokṣakāraṇamavyaktamacintyamaparigraham . .
samārādhya jagannāthaṃ kriyāyogena mucyate . . 19
1.61.d:
यस्माद्भिन्नमिदं सर्वं 3यच्चेदं यच्च नेङ्गति ।
मोक्षकारणमव्यक्तमचिन्त्यमपरिग्रहम् ॥
समाराध्य जगन्नाथं क्रियायोगेन मुच्यते ॥ 19
1.61.m:
from whom everything is distinct, both what moves and what does not move.
Having worshipped the Lord of the universe, the cause of liberation, unmanifest, unthinkable, without possessions,
through the yoga of action, one is liberated.'

1.61.s: iti te brahmaṇaḥ śrutvā rahasyamṛṣisattamāḥ . . 1.61.20
1.61.d: इति ते ब्रह्मणः श्रुत्वा रहस्यमृषिसत्तमाः ॥ 1.61.20
1.61.m: Having heard this secret from Brahmā, those best of sages

1.61.s:
narāṇāmupakārāya yogaśāstrāṇi cakrire .
kriyāyogaparāṇīha muktikārīṇyanekaśaḥ . . 21
1.61.d:
नराणामुपकाराय योगशास्त्राणि चक्रिरे ।
क्रियायोगपराणीह मुक्तिकारीण्यनेकशः ॥ 21
1.61.m:
composed treatises on yoga for the benefit of mankind,
focused here on the yoga of action, which effect liberation in many ways.

1.61.s:
ārādhyate jagannāthastadanuṣṭhānatatparaiḥ .
paramātmā sa mārtaṇḍaḥ sarveśaḥ sarvabhāvanaḥ . . 22
1.61.d:
आराध्यते जगन्नाथस्तदनुष्ठानतत्परैः ।
परमात्मा स मार्तण्डः सर्वेशः सर्वभावनः ॥ 22
1.61.m:
The Lord of the universe is worshipped by those intent on its practice;
he is the supreme self, Mārtaṇḍa, lord of all, the creator of all.

1.61.s:
yānyuktāni purā tena brahmaṇā kurunandana .
tāni te kuruśārdūla sarvapāpaharāṇyaham . . 23
1.61.d:
यान्युक्तानि पुरा तेन ब्रह्मणा कुरुनन्दन ।
तानि ते कुरुशार्दूल सर्वपापहराण्यहम् ॥ 23
1.61.m:
Those matters which were spoken formerly by Brahmā, O joy of the Kurus,
those destroying all sins, I shall now declare to you,

1.61.s:
vakṣyāmi śrūyatāmadya rahasyamidamuttamam .
saṃsārārṇavamagnānāṃ viṣayākrāṃtacetasām . . 24
1.61.d:
वक्ष्यामि श्रूयतामद्य रहस्यमिदमुत्तमम् ।
संसारार्णवमग्नानां विषयाक्रांतचेतसाम् ॥ 24
1.61.m:
O tiger of the Kurus; let this supreme secret be heard.
For those submerged in the ocean of worldly existence, whose minds are overcome by sense-objects,

1.61.s:
haṃsapotaṃ vinā nānyatkiṃcidasti parāyaṇam .
uttiṣṭhaṃściṃtaya raviṃ vrajaṃściṃtaya gopatim . . 25
1.61.d:
हंसपोतं विना नान्यत्किंचिदस्ति परायणम् ।
उत्तिष्ठंश्चिंतय रविं व्रजंश्चिंतय गोपतिम् ॥ 25
1.61.m:
there is no other refuge except the boat of the Sun.
While rising, contemplate the Sun; while walking, contemplate the Lord of rays;

1.61.s:
bhuñjaṃściṃtaya mārtaṃḍaṃ svapāṃściṃtaya bhāskaram .
evamekāgracittastvaṃ saṃśritaḥ satataṃ ravim . . 26
1.61.d:
भुञ्जंश्चिंतय मार्तंडं स्वपांश्चिंतय भास्करम् ।
एवमेकाग्रचित्तस्त्वं संश्रितः सततं रविम् ॥ 26
1.61.m:
while eating, contemplate Mārtaṇḍa; while sleeping, contemplate the Sun.
In this way, single-minded and constantly seeking refuge in the Sun,

1.61.s: janmamṛtyumahāgrāhaṃ saṃsārāmbhastariṣyasi . . 27
1.61.d: जन्ममृत्युमहाग्राहं संसाराम्भस्तरिष्यसि ॥ 27
1.61.m: you will cross the water of worldly existence infested with the great crocodiles of birth and death.

1.61.s:
graheśamīśaṃ varadaṃ purāṇaṃ jagadvidhātāramajaṃ ca nityam .
samāśritā ye ravimīśitāraṃ teṣāṃ bhavo nāsti vimuktibhājām . . 28
1.61.d:
ग्रहेशमीशं वरदं पुराणं जगद्विधातारमजं च नित्यम् ।
समाश्रिता ये रविमीशितारं तेषां भवो नास्ति विमुक्तिभाजाम् ॥ 28
1.61.m:
Those who take refuge in the Sun, the lord of the planets, the boon-giving ruler, ancient, creator of the world, unborn and eternal, the sovereign—
for them who attain liberation, rebirth does not exist.

1.61.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe
sūryayogamahimavarṇanaṃ nāmaikaṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 61 .
sūryadiṇḍīsaṃvādam
1.61.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे
सूर्ययोगमहिमवर्णनं नामैकषष्टितमोऽध्यायः । 61 ।
सूर्यदिण्डीसंवादम्
1.61.m:
Thus ends the sixty-first chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of the Yoga of the Sun', in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa consisting of fifty thousand verses.
Dialogue between the Sun and Diṇḍi
